title: W098 unified value model — CalcValue and callable rich
description: Design-of-record + cross-repo lane map for replacing OxFunc EvalValue with CalcValue { core: CoreValue, rich: Option<Rc<RichValue>> } (core + optional rich). CoreValue is the traditional Excel-compatible substrate (Number/Text/Logical/Error/Empty/Missing/Array/Reference); RichValue is the modern/extended payload layer. Callable values are RichValue::Callable(CallableValue { arity, summary, handle: Rc<dyn OpaqueCallable> }) with core: Error(#CALC!), carried by an opaque refcounted handle for TreeCalc node-as-function. The Rc is the lifetime (no token-map GC); OxFunc sees only arity/summary/handle; OxFml owns the concrete binding behind OpaqueCallable, including compiled-body cache handle/body, closure/value captures, invocation provenance, and captured-reference reporting. No persistence: callables rebuild from formulas. Existing structured rich payload folds into RichValue::Object(RichObjectValue), preserving string-keyed extensibility. Migration is big-bang (~5k EvalValue sites). Workset doc: docs/worksets/W098_UNIFIED_VALUE_MODEL_AND_CALLABLE_RICH.md. No code lands under W098 itself — design + tracking only; .beads owns execution. Kept cross-repo workstream beads (related, not folded/reparented): oxf-ahi7 (W2 OxFunc), fml-oh8.2 (W3 OxFml), calc-4vs8.73 (W4 OxCalc), dtc-z0i.8 (W5 DnaTreeCalc). title: ASINH/SQRTPI publish +Inf for finite in-domain args (overflow-guard drift)
description:
Surfaced by the W105 .1 cross-surface equivalence harness (crates/oxfunc_core/tests/unary_numeric_equivalence_law.rs, Law 3). Two unary kernels violate the 'every kernel whose raw result can be non-finite for a finite arg declares a non-PASS real_result_policy' invariant:

- ASINH(1e308): |x| + hypot(x,1) = 2e308 -> +Inf, then ln(+Inf) -> +Inf. True asinh(1e308) ~= 709.89 (finite). Carries PASS policy, so +Inf leaks unguarded across all three surfaces.
- SQRTPI(1e308): n*PI ~= 3.14e308 > f64::MAX -> +Inf before the sqrt. True sqrt(1e308*PI) ~= 1.77e154 (representable). Carries PASS policy.

These are pre-existing (not introduced by W105). The harness records them as ratcheted m_known_law3 exceptions (Law 3 prints them; if the drift is repaired the test fails until the stale exception is removed). Repair must FIRST verify the Excel-exact published value live (per 'never accept a divergence' doctrine): determine whether Excel returns the finite analytic value (=> fix the kernel's internal overflow, e.g. asinh via ln1p / sign(x)*(ln|x| + ln2) for large |x|; sqrtpi via sqrt(n)*sqrt(PI)) or #NUM! (=> change real_result_policy to FINITE). Then remove the corresponding m_known_law3 exception so the invariant is enforced again. NOT a blocker for the W105 epic.
close_reason: FIXED in commit 77431cf (asinh.rs, sqrtpi.rs, + .1 harness exception removal). Oracle-established (live Excel 16.0 build 20026) that Excel does NOT return the finite analytic value - it returns #NUM! when its internal intermediate overflows: ASINH #NUM! for |x| where x*x overflows (>sqrt(f64::MAX)~1.34e154, finite <=1.3e154); SQRTPI #NUM! for n where n*PI overflows (>f64::MAX/PI~5.72e307). This was a WIDER divergence than the bead/harness assumed (OxFunc returned finite across 1.34e154<|x|<9e307 where Excel #NUM!s, not just +Inf at 1e308). FIX (kernel-level, both Fallible): compute the SAME intermediate Excel forms (x*x / n*PI) and return Num iff non-finite - reproduces Excel's EXACT boundary via identical f64 arithmetic (no magic constant). SUPERVISOR-VERIFIED bit-exact via independent OxFunc-vs-oracle differential: ASINH 1.3e154/1e150 finite bit-identical, 1.4e154/1e308 #NUM; SQRTPI 5.72e307/1e10 finite bit-identical, 5.8e307/1e308 #NUM - all match Excel. The 2 stale m_known_law3 exceptions REMOVED (ratchet-intended; constructor kept as escape hatch with #[allow(dead_code)]); Law 3 now enforces the invariant on ASINH/SQRTPI; harness 6/6. real_result_policy unchanged (PASS), FunctionMeta Eq/Copy intact. Build zero-warnings; .1 6/6 + .2 1/1 + .10 golden green; lib 1472; only HO-FN-018 red. Residual: 1-ULP SQRTPI gap at the single n*PI=f64::MAX boundary input -> tracked separately.

At the single input n = f64::MAX/PI (bits 0x7fd45f306dc9c882), n*PI rounds to exactly f64::MAX (finite, so NOT the overflow #NUM! case - both Excel and OxFunc return finite here). But OxFunc sqrt(f64::MAX) publishes 0x5fefffffffffffff while Excel publishes 0x5ff0000000000000 - a 1-ULP difference at that one boundary input. Orthogonal to the oxf-7m1k overflow-guard fix (which is complete and bit-exact elsewhere). Per the ULP doctrine (Excel imprecision is still a bug; match Excel) this is a tracked divergence. Extremely edge (one input); low priority. Likely Excel computes sqrt(n*PI) with a different rounding of the n*PI product or the sqrt. Not a blocker.
close_reason: FIXED in commit (sqrtpi.rs): root cause is NOT x87/extended precision (64-bit Excel + Rust are both SSE2) - Excel computes SQRTPI(n)=(n*PI)^0.5 via its pow routine, not the IEEE correctly-rounded sqrt. The two agree at normal magnitudes but diverge 1 ULP at scattered near-overflow points (the bead's single-input premise was too narrow: at least 0x7fd45f306dc9c880 AND 0x7fd45f306dc9c882 diverge). FIX: kernel uses product.powf(0.5) instead of product.sqrt() (overflow->#NUM! guard preserved). SUPERVISOR-VERIFIED bit-exact: independent oracle sweep of 30 inputs across the full magnitude range (.tmp/sqrtpi-broad-oracle.ps1 + sqrtpi-boundary-oracle.ps1, live Excel 16.0 build 20026) - powf(0.5) matches Excel 30/30 incl. both previously-divergent points; sqrt matched 28/30. Fixed kernel re-checked 12/12 vs Excel. Boundary test updated to pin 0x5ff0000000000000. .1 harness 6/6, SQRTPI suite 3/3, lib 1472, only HO-FN-018 red. NOTE: the pow-vs-sqrt finding may generalize - other Excel functions computed via pow/exp/log (rather than a dedicated correctly-rounded op) could have the same scattered-1-ULP signature; worth bearing in mind for future near-boundary ULP investigations.

title: Array-lifter does not lift a 1x1-array arg (treats it as scalar); Excel lifts it
description:
Oracle-established (W105 .12.2 investigation; .tmp/reshape-lift-oracle2.ps1, live Excel 16.0 build 20026). At an observed_scalar_array_lift position, OxFunc treats a 1x1 array arg as a SCALAR (unwraps it) and returns the function's full result, whereas Excel LIFTS the 1x1 array (implicit-intersection broadcast -> a single intersected cell).

Witnessed cases (Excel vs OxFunc):
- EXPAND({1,2;3,4},{3},2,0): Excel 1x1=[1]  vs OxFunc 3x2=[1,2,3,4,0,0]
- TOROW({1,2;3,4},{0}):      Excel 1x1=[1]  vs OxFunc 1x4=[1,2,3,4]
- DROP({1,2,3;4,5,6},{1}):   Excel 1x1=[4]  (OxFunc currently #VALUE! via calc-dispatch; after W105 .12.2 collapse it lifts like EXPAND/TOROW and will hit THIS same 1x1 residual)
MULTI-element array counts already MATCH Excel exactly (e.g. {3;4} -> 2x1=[1,1] both), so the lift mechanism is fundamentally right - only the 1x1-array case unwraps-to-scalar. Likely affects ALL functions carrying an observed-lift mask, not just the reshape family.

Per W105-D2 the [1,2] lift mask is a CORRECT declared Excel fact and stays; this is a defect in the shared array-lifter (try_observed_scalar_array_lift / the values-only prep), NOT the spec. Fix: lift a 1x1 array at a lift position rather than unwrapping it to scalar. Per user (2026-06-22): not disruptive to fix after the FunctionSpec work lands; tracked here so it is not forgotten. NOT a blocker for W105.
close_reason: FIXED in commit 06efc82 (adapters.rs + surface_dispatch.rs). Oracle-established (live Excel 16.0 build 20026) the precise rule: a 1x1-array arg {e} at an observed-lift position is LIFTED -> f(e) implicit-intersected (top-left) -> returned as a SCALAR. Bug was specific to ARRAY-returning observed-lift fns (EXPAND/DROP/TAKE/TOROW/MUNIT): OxFunc unwrapped {e}->e and returned the FULL array, where Excel returns the intersected scalar; scalar-returning fns (NORMSDIST/NORMDIST/PERCENTILE/ADDRESS/dist/IM*/...) already matched (intersection of a scalar = that scalar). FIX (shared lifter): non-collapsing prep + treat any array (incl 1x1) at a lift position as a lift array, collapse a 1x1 lifted result to a bare scalar; added a narrow dispatch arm routing the 1x1-array case through the lifter. SUPERVISOR-VERIFIED via independent OxFunc-vs-oracle differential: (i) EXPAND({3})->1, DROP({1})->20, TAKE({2})->10, TOROW({0})->1, MUNIT({2})->1 now MATCH Excel; (ii) NORMSDIST({0})->0.5, PERCENTILE(,{0.5})->2.5 UNCHANGED; (iii) multi-element DROP(,{0;1})->2x1=[1,4] UNCHANGED; (iv) scalar arg MUNIT(2)->2x2 UNCHANGED. title: W093 remove OxFunc INDIRECT local reference-text fallback
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Call OxFunc INDIRECT with argument text such as `"A1"` or `"Sheet1!A1"` through `eval_indirect_surface` while the `FunctionExecutionContext` has no `reference_text_resolver`. Before this corrective bead, OxFunc parsed A1/R1C1-like text locally and returned a `ReferenceLike` instead of requiring the host-provided reference-text resolver.

## Bug
OxFunc INDIRECT must not parse A1/R1C1 or any host reference text locally when no FEC reference-text resolver is present. INDIRECT should be an ordinary OxFunc function that asks `FunctionExecutionContext.reference_text_resolver` to resolve argument text into `ReferenceLike`. If the capability is absent, return a typed `ReferenceTextResolutionError::Unsupported` mapped to `#REF`. No TreeCalc, Excel-grid, A1, R1C1, or future host syntax parsing belongs in OxFunc for INDIRECT.
acceptance_criteria: 1. eval_indirect_surface requires a FunctionExecutionContext reference-text resolver for all reference text resolution. 2. Missing reference_text_resolver returns ReferenceTextResolutionError::Unsupported mapped to #REF. 3. Legacy A1/R1C1 fallback tests are removed or rewritten to prove no local parsing occurs. 4. OxFunc full library tests pass. 5. OxFml supplies a reference-text resolver in tests that need successful INDIRECT resolution; no-host tests assert typed failure where no resolver is present.
close_reason: Product status: OxFunc INDIRECT no longer has a local A1/R1C1 or host-reference text fallback. It requires FunctionExecutionContext.reference_text_resolver for all dynamic reference-text resolution and maps an absent resolver to ReferenceTextResolutionError::Unsupported/#REF. Evidence: cargo fmt --check --manifest-path crates/oxfunc_core/Cargo.toml; cargo test --manifest-path crates/oxfunc_core/Cargo.toml --lib; git diff --check; br lint oxf-ypq2.18; br dep cycles; fresh-eyes review accepted closure.

## Goal

Replace confusing `Surface*` execution names with names that distinguish formula-visible surface names from resolved function targets, per-call execution context, scratch storage, and expression hoist policy.
